scope: NIC interrupt (Broadcom tg3 INTx through the Apple PCIe root port and the AIC3) from nothing to the board default
source: snapshot of the hop-os working tree with local hop and lean; toolchain with patch 0003

facts.aic: aic,3 version 0xa at 0x381000000; 2048 of 4096 interrupts; config words +0x10000, event +0x40000, global config +0x14 (bit 0 off at boot); iBoot leaves every mask set and no targets
facts.msi: doorbell 0xfffff000, vector offset 1506, port 2 vector base 64 (1570..1601); no port register at +0x2000/+0x2800/+0x160 holds the doorbell; firmware MSI map entry at +0x3000 reads 0x80000200; enabling MSI without a decode took the node down (bundle 18) — MSI not used
facts.intx: apcie "interrupts" = 1231, 1240, 1249 (one block of nine per port); INTA of port 2 is 1253 (base + 4), found by delivery; INTMSK +0x104 = 0xfffffff0 leaves INTA..D through; INTSTAT +0x100 is read-only: a write-one-to-clear is a synchronous external abort (ESR 0x96000410, FAR 0x492028100)
facts.tg3: INTA# asserted once MISC_HOST_CTRL.MASK_PCI_INT is cleared and the interrupt mailbox holds 0 (PCI status bit 3, status word 0x3); ack = mailbox 1 (line drops), rearm = mailbox 0 from WaitNIC after the pump round
facts.target: AIC config target 0 delivers to HOP core MPIDR 0x10100 (found with a software-raised interrupt)
facts.masks: only PSTATE.I is opened (idle.ServeIRQ); F stays masked because the Apple timer FIQ wakes WFI without ever being taken

bundles.change: AIC3 driver + I-only service loop + tg3 MSI + Apple wiring with target scan and MSI discovery (DefaultNICIRQ=auto)
16 + t8122 MSI map at port+0x3000, whole-window discovery scan, soft-irq ack clears
17 + tg3 IRQUnmask clears MASK_PCI_INT; MSI detection by delivery over the whole window
18 + MSI only after a port doorbell register is found by write/readback (0x2000, 0x2800, 0x160); port register dump
19 + wiring 15 s after boot in a goroutine, 1.5 s pause after each risky step so the console shows the last step before a crash
INTx instead of MSI: port irq from the bridge "interrupts" prop, ack = tg3 mailbox + INTSTAT W1C
21 + port irq from the apcie "interrupts" prop indexed by port
22 + INTx diagnostics (tg3 status word, HOSTCC, PCI status bit 3) and a 30-line neighbour scan
23 + neighbour acks record only; hardware ack replayed step by step in the wiring goroutine; ESR/FAR/PC on EL1 exceptions
INTx: scan port lines base..base+8 with counting ack, ack = tg3 mailbox mask only (no INTSTAT write), rearm in WaitNIC
FINAL M4: 25 with DefaultNICIRQ=auto as the Apple default, no LDX

measurements.fixture: Vitals, 2 cores, 512 MiB; rtt/storm from this Mac over 1 Gbit; 64 MiB upload (HOP RX) and download (HOP TX) via /sink and /blob; rx = 32 MB from the internet

final.console: irq: NIC INTx on AIC irq 1253 (root port 2) routed to target 0 — RX wakes on the interrupt

incidents: bundle 18: node dark (MSI enabled with the chip interrupt mask cleared and no doorbell decode); watchdog recovery
bundle 23/24: EL1 exception in the ack (INTSTAT write), SError storm; after bundle 24 the node hung with ping alive, no agent, no watchdog reset; macvdmtool reboot worked only the next morning
the kis debug channel is lost on every reboot: re-enable with macvdmtool debugusb per attempt

the installed kernel refuses a FLIP over a resident with different switch code: empty the node first; the embedded config re-seeds welcome on port 80, which collides with spin — remove welcome before restoring spin
open: no idle wake-rate measurement on the M4 (polling was 3333 wakes/s; now one wake per frame plus the 10 ms guard)
one rx download of 32 MB from the internet ended in "unexpected EOF" after 586 s on bundle 25; the repeat and the local 64 MiB transfers passed; not attributed
the AIC IRQ_CFG target semantics are measured, not documented: target 0 reached HOP's core
watchdog did not reset the node after the bundle 24 panic; the exit path is suspected of disarming it
